T|/sys.rows/1/2: Seals the inserted packers and the crack zone on the surface, approx. 15 cm wide.
T|/sys.rows/2/2: Plugs the boreholes flush with the surface after the packers are removed. Consumption approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm layer thickness.
T|/sys.rows/3/1: Injection hose for waterproofing of construction joints
T|/sys.rows/3/2: {P4} is a system component of this injection hose for the internal waterproofing of construction joints in concrete structures.

STEPS[0]|/short: Quality class, temperature and moisture decide whether the injection can start.
STEPS[0]|/overview: Check the component before work starts. The technical data sheet sets minimum substrate quality classes and temperature limits for {P4}.
STEPS[0]|/points/0: concrete: min. C20/25, tensile adhesion strength ≥ 1.5 N/mm², age min. 28 days
STEPS[0]|/points/1: screed: min. CT-C35-F5, tensile adhesion strength ≥ 1.5 N/mm²
STEPS[0]|/points/2: plaster: min. P IIIa / P IIIb, tensile adhesion strength ≥ 0.8 N/mm²
STEPS[0]|/points/3: substrate temperature approx. 5–30 °C, application temperature approx. 10–30 °C
STEPS[0]|/points/4: suitable on dry and damp substrates
STEPS[0]|/warning: In the event of water-conducting cracks, an initial injection of {P1} is necessary to stop the ingress of water!
STEPS[0]|/note: Protect surfaces that are not to be treated from the effects of {P4}!
STEPS[1]|/short: Drill the injection holes, then clear the debris with oil-free compressed air.
STEPS[1]|/overview: Drill the injection holes to suit the injection packers. Clear any drilling debris in the drilled holes using oil-free compressed air.
STEPS[1]|/points/0: drilling pattern, hole diameter and spacing according to the project specification and the packer used
STEPS[1]|/points/2: holes free of drilling debris before the packers are inserted
STEPS[2]|/short: One injection packer in each cleared hole.
STEPS[2]|/overview: Insert the injection packer into each cleared hole.
STEPS[2]|/points/0: packer to suit the grouting device: hand lever press, foot lever press or mechanical grouting system
STEPS[2]|/points/1: all packers inserted before the surface is sealed
STEPS[3]|/short: Seal packers and the zone of the {defect} approx. 15 cm wide with ASODUR-EKF.
STEPS[3]|/overview: Seal the inserted packers and the zone of the {defect} on the surface approx. 15 cm wide with {EKF}.
STEPS[3]|/points/0: sealing width approx. 15 cm over the zone of the {defect}, packers included
STEPS[3]|/points/1: allow the crack insulation to cure before grouting
STEPS[4]|/short: 1 : 1 by volume, approx. 3 minutes, then decant and stir again.
STEPS[4]|/overview: {P4} is a 2 component system, mixed 1 volume share component A to 1 volume share component B with a stirrer at approx. 300 rpm.
STEPS[4]|/points/0: store the material at +15 °C for 12 hours before use
STEPS[4]|/points/1: add the hardener to the resin
STEPS[4]|/points/2: the hardener must run completely out of the container
STEPS[4]|/points/3: mix thoroughly with the mixer until a homogeneous consistency is achieved
STEPS[4]|/points/5: decant the mass into a clean bucket
STEPS[4]|/warning: Higher temperatures shorten the pot life. Lower temperatures increase the application and hardening times!
STEPS[5]|/short: After the surface seal has cured, grout in the mixed AQUAFIN-P4.
STEPS[5]|/overview: After the crack insulation has cured, grout in the thoroughly mixed {P4} using a grouting device.
STEPS[5]|/points/0: aids: hand lever press, foot lever press, suitable injection equipment, mechanical grouting system (piston pump or airless)
STEPS[5]|/points/2: consumption approx. 1.1 kg per litre of voids
STEPS[5]|/points/3: machine application: see the additional Technical Information No. 43
STEPS[5]|/note: The rate at which material is consumed also increases at lower temperatures.
STEPS[6]|/short: After curing, remove the packers and plug flush with ASOCRET-M30.
STEPS[6]|/overview: After the resin has cured, remove the injection packers and plug the boreholes flush with the surface using {M30}.
STEPS[7]|/short: Clean immediately with suitable solvent. Store at 15–25 °C.
STEPS[7]|/overview: Clean tools immediately after use with suitable solvent. The injection system must be cleaned at the end of work or in case of a longer interruption to work.
STEPS[7]|/points/0: no material residues shall be allowed to dry and stick in the equipment
STEPS[7]|/points/1: the cleaning agent or solvent must have a flash point above +21 °C
STEPS[7]|/points/2: observe the specifications of the respective machine manufacturer
STEPS[7]|/points/3: store frost-free, cool and dry, at 15–25 °C, for 12 months in the original canister
SCN.wall|/problem: A crack runs through the full thickness of a reinforced concrete wall. Moisture, or water, reaches the accessible side.
SCN.wall|/solution: Holes are drilled every 20 cm on alternating sides of the crack, at 45°, so that every hole crosses the crack inside the wall. {EKF} seals the crack on the surface; {P4} is grouted in from the lowest packer upwards.
SCN.hjoint|/problem: A horizontal joint between two pours, or a horizontal crack, lets water through along its whole length.
SCN.hjoint|/solution: Drill packers are set alternately above and below the joint; every hole crosses the joint at 45°. The joint is sealed on the surface with {EKF} and grouted packer by packer with {P4}.
SCN.hjoint|/caps/intro: Reinforced concrete wall with a horizontal construction joint
SCN.hjoint|/caps/leak: Moisture comes through along the joint, the surface below it gets damp
SCN.wfjoint|/problem: The joint between the floor slab and the wall cast onto it is the classic leak of a basement: ground water follows the joint to the inside.
SCN.wfjoint|/solution: Holes are drilled from the wall face at 45° downwards, so that they cross the joint under the wall. Joint and packers are sealed with {EKF}; {P4} spreads along the joint from packer to packer. In new construction the injection hose {CJ1} is cast into this joint and injected with {P1} or {P4}.
SCN.wfjoint|/caps/intro: Wall cast onto the floor slab: the construction joint at its foot
SCN.wfjoint|/caps/leak: Ground water follows the joint to the inside
SCN.honeycomb|/note: Schematic, not to scale. Holes at 45° into the gravel pocket; number of holes, hole diameter and packer type according to the project specification.
SCN.honeycomb|/problem: Poorly compacted concrete at the foot of a wall: coarse aggregate with too little cement paste between the grains. The pocket is permeable over its whole depth.
SCN.honeycomb|/solution: Holes are drilled at 45° into the pocket, its surface is sealed with {EKF}, and the low-viscosity {P4} is grouted in until the space between the grains is filled. Where water flows, {P1} stops it first.
SCN.honeycomb|/caps/intro: Gravel pocket at the foot of the wall
SCN.honeycomb|/caps/leak: Water passes through the pocket, the surface gets damp
SCN.honeycomb|/caps/inject: Grout in AQUAFIN-P4: the resin fills the space between the grains
SCN.honeycomb|/steps/0/0: Drill into the pocket, clear the holes
SCN.honeycomb|/steps/0/1: Drill the injection holes at 45° into the gravel pocket. Clear any drilling debris using oil-free compressed air.
SCN.pipe|/problem: The ring joint between a pipe or shaft and the concrete cast around it leaks: the two materials shrink and move differently.
SCN.pipe|/solution: Holes are set around the pipe and drilled at 45° towards the joint. The ring joint is sealed on the surface with {EKF} and grouted packer by packer around the pipe. {P4} adheres to both flanks and cures to soft elastic.
SCN.pipe|/caps/intro: Pipe passing through a reinforced concrete slab
SCN.pipe|/caps/leak: Water rises through the ring joint around the pipe
SCN.slab|/problem: A crack through a floor slab with ground water below it, for example under a station building or in a basement floor.
SCN.slab|/solution: The crack is injected from the top: holes at 45° on alternating sides, surface seal with {EKF}, then {P4}. If water wells up through the crack, {P1} stops it first.
SCN.slab|/caps/intro: Reinforced concrete floor slab with a continuous crack
SCN.slab|/caps/leak: Ground water rises through the crack, the surface gets damp
SCN.dam|/problem: Basins, tanks, retaining walls and dams with water standing against one side. The crack conducts water under pressure.
SCN.dam|/solution: The work is done from the dry side. {P1} is injected first: it reacts with the water, foams and stops the ingress. {P4} follows as the elastic, crack-bridging seal.
SCN.dam|/caps/intro: Basin wall with water standing behind it
SCN.dam|/caps/leak: Water is pressed through the crack
SCN.sewer|/problem: Ground water infiltrates through cracks and joints of the sewer wall, or sewage escapes through them.
SCN.sewer|/solution: Injection from inside the sewer: holes at 45° on alternating sides of the crack. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} follows for the permanent, elastic waterproofing of the crack.
SCN.sewer|/caps/intro: Sewer wall with a longitudinal crack
SCN.sewer|/caps/leak: Ground water infiltrates through the crack
SCN.manhole|/problem: Inspection chambers and manhole shafts built in lifts or from rings: ground water enters through the joints between the lifts or rings and round the pipe connections; the chamber runs full at high water.
SCN.manhole|/solution: Injection from inside the shaft, the flow diverted first: holes at 45° alternately above and below the joint so that each hole crosses it inside the wall. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} follows as the permanent, elastic seal of the joint.
SCN.manhole|/caps/intro: Manhole shaft cast in lifts: the construction joint between two lifts
SCN.manhole|/caps/leak: Ground water enters along the joint between the lifts
SCN.cutcover|/problem: A rectangular tunnel cast in an open excavation: the construction joints between base slab and walls and between walls and roof, and the joints between the pours along the tunnel, are where the ground water comes in.
SCN.cutcover|/solution: From inside the tunnel, in a lane closure: holes drilled from the wall face at 45° downwards so that they cross the wall–base joint under the wall. {P1} stops the water, the joint and the packers are sealed with {EKF}, and {P4} spreads along the joint from packer to packer.
SCN.cutcover|/caps/intro: Cut-and-cover tunnel: the construction joint at the foot of the side wall
SCN.cutcover|/caps/leak: Ground water follows the joint into the tunnel
SCN.tbm|/problem: A tunnel bored by a tunnel boring machine and lined with precast concrete segments: water finds the ring joints and the longitudinal joints where a gasket is damaged or a segment is offset, and the bolt pockets and grout holes.
SCN.tbm|/solution: From inside the tunnel: the bolt pockets and the gasket groove are located first, then holes are drilled at 45° to the joint between them so that each hole meets the joint plane inside the segment. {P1} stops the inflow, {P4} seals the joint elastically. The gasket itself stays untouched.
SCN.tbm|/caps/intro: Segmental lining of a TBM tunnel: the longitudinal joint between two segments of a ring
SCN.tbm|/caps/leak: Ground water enters through the longitudinal joint and the bolt pockets
SCN.shield|/problem: A metro tunnel driven by a shield in soft, water-bearing ground: the ground water stands high against the segmental lining and enters at ring joints and longitudinal joints where the gasket no longer seals, along cracks in the segments and at the grout holes.
SCN.shield|/solution: From the walkway, outside operating hours: holes at 45° to the joint on alternating sides, clear of the bolts and the gasket groove. {P1} first, until the inflow stops, then {P4} for the permanent elastic seal. Pressures kept low: the resin must fill the joint, not lift the lining.
SCN.shield|/caps/intro: Shield tunnel in soft ground: the segmental lining with its ring joint
SCN.shield|/caps/leak: Ground water under pressure enters through the ring joint
SCN.immersed|/problem: Tunnel elements cast in a dry dock, floated out and sunk into a dredged trench. The immersion joint is sealed by the Gina gasket outside and the Omega seal inside; where an element wall has cracked, or the joint zone leaks past the concrete, water enters under the head of the sea or river above.
SCN.immersed|/solution: From inside the tunnel: cracks in the element and the concrete joint zone are injected at 45° on alternating sides; the rubber seals are never drilled. {P1} stops the water, {P4} gives the elastic, watertight seal of the crack.
SCN.immersed|/caps/intro: Immersed tube tunnel: the element joint with its Omega seal, a crack beside it
SCN.immersed|/caps/leak: Water under the head above enters through the crack
SCN.adhesive|/note: Schematic, crack width exaggerated. Packer spacing and injection pressure according to the project specification.
SCN.adhesive|/problem: Thin components, dense reinforcement or prestressing steel do not allow drilling. The crack is dry or damp.
SCN.adhesive|/solution: Adhesive packers are bonded over the crack with {EKF}, the crack between them is sealed, and the resin is grouted in at low pressure through the packers. {P4} gives the elastic, watertight seal; for a force-locking bond of dry cracks in concrete: {IH} (not for statically relevant areas).
SCN.adhesive|/caps/intro: Crack in a component that must not be drilled
SCN.adhesive|/caps/drill: Clean the crack zone with oil-free compressed air
SCN.adhesive|/caps/air: Clean the crack zone with oil-free compressed air
SCN.adhesive|/caps/packer: Bond the adhesive packers over the crack
SCN.adhesive|/caps/seal: Seal the crack between the packers with ASODUR-EKF
SCN.adhesive|/caps/done: Crack sealed without a single drilled hole
SCN.adhesive|/steps/0/1: Remove loose parts, dust and laitance along the crack and blow the zone off with oil-free compressed air. Nothing is drilled.
SCN.adhesive|/steps/1/1: Bond the packers centrally over the crack with {EKF}. The crack must stay open under each packer.
SCN.adhesive|/steps/2/0: Seal the crack between the packers
SCN.adhesive|/steps/2/1: Seal the crack on the surface between and around the packers with {EKF}. Allow the crack insulation to cure.
SCN.adhesive|/steps/4/1: After the resin has cured, remove the adhesive packers. The surface seal can be removed as necessary for visual reasons.
SCN.adhesive|/modelA: Adhesive packers need a dry or damp crack that does not conduct water: the adhesive must bond to the surface.
SCN_T|/title: Where it leaks, and how it is sealed
SCN_T|/sub: Select the situation on site. The 3D mechanism, the five steps and the cross-section follow your choice.
